drivers.label: CCPG (client) revenue
drivers.source: Actuals: segment tables of the releases [16][15][13][17] (FY2026 Q1-Q3, FY2025 quarters); quarter shape from three filed years, each on one basis: FY2023 5,767 / 6,780 / 7,867 / 8,844 (Q1 2024 release [src 68], Q3 2024 [22], Q4 2024 [21]: FY2023 29,258, Q2 the remainder), FY2024 recast for the NEX integration 8,273 / 8,143 / 8,161 / 8,769 (prior-year columns of the Q1-Q4 2025 releases [20][19][18][17], FY2024 33,346), FY2025 7,629 / 7,871 / 8,535 / 8,193 [17]. Q3 2026 call [src 42], David Zinsner (CFO): 'We expect CCPG revenue to decline greater than 20% sequentially'; 'For 2027, we're planning for the PC unit TAM to decline roughly 10%'; 'We expect year-over-year declines to be more pronounced during the first half'; 'we'll see somewhat of a seasonal decline next quarter'; 'And then we'll have to see in '28 whether things improve'; 'we're in a kind of a market share gain type of environment for our clients'. BofA Q4 PC shipments -25% to -30% q/q [src 25]. PC units: IDC Q3 2026 62.7M, -20.1% y/y [src 61]; Q1 65.6M (+2.5%) [src 66], Q2 68.2M (-4.9%) [src 67], Q4 2025 76.4M [src 65]; IDC outlook (updated 2026-10-30) [src 60]: 2026 -11.3%, 2027 -3.1%, 2028 +2.0%, 2029 +2.6% (PCs + tablets; slates 'forecast to edge down'); Omdia (2026-10-09) [src 62]: Q4 2026 -24% y/y, 2027 -7%; Omdia US (2026-09-10) [src 63]: no return to growth before 2028. Share: Mercury Q2 2026 Intel client 69.7% [src 53]; Q3 2026 desktop 70.1% (+5.0 pts, supply shifted from laptops), total x86 66.1%, ~3 pts lower y/y [src 64].
drivers.derivation: Q4 FY26 6,073 = Q3 8,097 x (1 - 25%): BofA puts Q4 PC shipments down 25-30% q/q [src 25]; the less severe end because the edge business 'was more resilient' (Zinsner, CFO [src 42]); inside the CFO's 'greater than 20%'. FY27 27,697 = FY26 30,774 x 0.90: the CFO's ~-10% 2027 unit TAM [src 42] with share and ASP/mix netted flat; newer outside forecasts sit above it (Omdia -7% [src 62], IDC -3.1% [src 60], IDC's from before Q3), so the CFO's is the moderately conservative one. Quarters: Q1 5,395 = Q4 x 0.8883, the mean Q1/Q4 ratio of three years on one basis each (7,533/8,844 = 0.852 [src 68][21], 7,629/8,769 = 0.870 [20][17], 7,727/8,193 = 0.943 [16][17]; the earlier 0.9435 mixed pre- and post-recast quarters); Q3 and Q4 at the consumption level C and Q2 halfway between Q1 and C (CFO: declines 'more pronounced during the first half'): Q1 + (Q1 + C)/2 + 2C = 27,697 gives C = 7,842, Q2 6,618. FY28 ground-up = consumption level x PC units x Intel unit share x ASP/mix, quarter by quarter a year on: H2 FY28 = 2C x 1.020 (IDC 2028 units +2.0% [src 60]; the first growth year in IDC, Omdia US [src 63]; IDC's figure includes tablets, whose slates edge down, so PCs alone run slightly higher: kept at 2.0%, moderately conservative) x 1.00 share x 1.00 ASP/mix; share netted flat: management expects gains with Nova Lake ('we go into the year as a market share gainer with our Nova Lake portfolio', David Zinsner, CFO; 'As the market normalizes, we expect this portfolio drives meaningful share gains', Lip-Bu Tan, CEO [src 42]) while Mercury shows Intel ~3 pts lower y/y in total x86 and its Q3 desktop gain came from supply moved off laptops [src 64]; ASP/mix netted flat: better high-end desktop mix ('we should see better traction on the high-end desktop', Zinsner, CFO) against the low-end Wildcat Lake ramp ('increased units by approximately 70% sequentially', Zinsner, CFO [src 42]); share is sized as alternatives (Mercury-pace loss, Nova Lake gain), while ASP/mix is netted flat with no quantified source (no cited page sizes a 2027-28 ASP or mix change), so no ASP/mix alternative is built. FY28 52-week level = H2 / 0.5327 (Q3+Q4 share of the three-year shape [0.2273, 0.2401, 0.2595, 0.2732]) = 30,035; quarters on that shape, Q1 x 14/13 for the 53-week FY2028: 7,352 / 7,210 / 7,794 / 8,204 = 30,560 (+10.3% on FY27: +2.0% units, +1.9% the extra week, the rest billings back to consumption after the H1 FY27 inventory correction). FY29 = FY28 52-week level x 1.026 (IDC 2029 +2.6% [src 60]), same shape, 52 weeks: 30,815; outside the NTM window at the horizon, so it carries no value. Reconciled to actuals: IDC PC units 2026 YTD -8.3% (65.6 + 68.2 + 62.7 = 196.5M vs 64.0 + 71.7 + 78.5 = 214.2M [src 66][src 67][src 61]); IDC's 2026 desktops -12.4% / notebooks -11.3% [src 60] (about -11.5% for PCs on 2025's 290.6M with Q4 2025 76.4M [src 65]) then need Q4 at about -21% y/y, between IDC's earlier -20% and Omdia's post-Q3 -24% [src 62], so the IDC path still holds after Q3; CCPG's Q4 at -25.9% y/y (6,073 vs 8,193) sits below both, as OEMs cut weeks of inventory (CFO [src 42]).

KILIAN CARD 2026-11-24 (cmsg_01HdhANNPxz1f5xqDwR22cfLFzsG6GiNiCEnTZngJoQmX1, 'Median of revised five 36.0B / 41.0B'): median of the five revised forecasters' DCAI builds (round 2, 2026-11-24); share loss to Arm and AMD: TrendForce 2026-10-22 [src 83] (server CPU units more than +40% in 2027, Arm ~30%, AMD rising, Intel share down on constrained supply), Mercury x86 shares via Wccftech [src 84]; substrate equipment lead times up to 30 months (S.C. Chien, Unimicron Chairman, TrendForce 2026-10-20 [src 92]); Intel 3 constraint and the +40% substrate capacity mostly in H2 2027 [src 42].

FY2027-29: KILIAN CARD 2026-11-24 (cmsg_01HdhANNPxz1f5xqDwR22cfLFzsG6GiNiCEnTZngJoQmX1, 'Median of revised five 36.0B / 41.0B'): the combined build of the five revised forecasters (round 2, 2026-11-24) replaces the supply-only build (the +40% substrate capacity phased in from H2 2027 with no share loss). Chien, Unimicron Chairman, a supplier, TrendForce 2026-10-20 [src 92]). drivers.label: CCPG operating margin (segment operating income / revenue)
drivers.source: Actuals: segment operating income / revenue, release segment tables [16][15][13][17]. Q3 2026 call [src 42], David Zinsner (CFO): 'CCPG operating profit was $2.3 billion, representing 28% of revenue'; 'I still lean towards the 40% to 60% fall-through'; 'The sequential decline in Q4 gross margin primarily reflects lower overall revenue against our fixed cost base'; Panther Lake gross margins 'not yet at or above the corporate average', 'these will be accretive gross margins over time'; 'Since Q1, Intel 18A client CPUs have grown from less than 5% of revenue to now nearly 1/3 of client CPU revenue'.
drivers.derivation: Cost model fitted to Q3 FY26 (cost 8,097 - 2,285 = 5,812 = 0.55 x revenue + ~1,350 fixed a 13-week quarter): a 45% incremental margin, the middle of the CFO's 40-60% fall-through [src 42]; margin = 0.45 - 1,350 x weeks/13 / revenue, less a Panther Lake mix deduction. Q4 FY26 21.8% (kept): 0.45 - 1,350 / 6,073 = 22.8% less ~1pt Panther Lake mix (CFO: 'not yet at or above the corporate average'). FY27 on revenue 5,395 / 6,618 / 7,842 / 7,842: 19.0% / 23.6% / 26.8% / 26.8% (less 1pt: 18A client parts at nearly a third of client CPU revenue and rising, still below the corporate average); FY28 24.7% / 25.8% / 27.2% / 28.0% (Q1 carries 14 weeks of fixed cost; less 0.5pt as Panther Lake margins move toward 'accretive over time'); FY29 25.7% / 26.8% / 28.1% / 29.0% (no mix deduction; outside the NTM window, no value effect). The earlier 1-2pt extra deduction for '18A client parts carry higher wafer cost than Intel 7' had no source and is removed.

drivers.source: Actuals: release segment tables [16][15][13][17]. Q4 non-GAAP GM guide 38% incl. ~200bp Fab 28 mostly on 10nm server [13][23]. Call [src 42]: Granite Rapids now margin accretive; purpose-built silicon margins below the corporate average, 'tripling over the last 3 years, and poised to triple again over the next few years' (Lip-Bu Tan, CEO), 'may put a little pressure on the operating margin percentage through next year'; industry supply-constrained through 2027 and into 2028; 18A underloading a headwind.
drivers.derivation: Q4 FY26 37.8% = Q3 41.5% less 3.7pt: the Fab 28 hit, 'an impact of roughly $300 million to revenue and 200 basis points to gross margin' (David Zinsner, CFO [src 42]), is 200bp x ~15.5B = ~$310M and lands almost all on 10nm server, so 310 / 8,416 = 3.7pt of DCAI margin. Two unsized forces are left out on both sides: custom-silicon mix, which 'may put a little pressure on the operating margin percentage through next year' (Zinsner, CFO [src 42]), and operating leverage on the +15% revenue. PREVIOUS (to the gate fix 2026-11-19): 35% as 'Q3 less ~5pt', which did not compute from its own parts. FY27 36% / 38% / 39% / 39% (Kilian card 2026-11-17 'Keep 36-39%'): the CFO expects the Fab 28 revenue hit to be 'similar in the first quarter' but the margin effect to be 'really more of a Q4 event' (Zinsner, CFO [src 42]), so Q1's 36% rests on the custom-silicon mix pressure through 2027 (unsized; owner-decided level); Granite Rapids 'is now margin accretive' (Zinsner, CFO [src 42]) carries Q2-Q4. PREVIOUS (to Kilian's card 2026-11-19): FY28 38% and FY29 38% (gate round 2 must-card, carded 2026-11-19): purpose-built silicon, with margins 'below the corporate average' (Zinsner, CFO [src 24]) and 'poised to triple again over the next few years' (Lip-Bu Tan, CEO [src 42]), keeps outgrowing DCAI, against Granite Rapids accretion and supply-tight pricing (industry 'supply-constrained throughout 2027 and into 2028', Zinsner [src 42]); the booked level is net about the FY2027 average (38.1%) and no source sizes it. The CFO puts the mix pressure only 'through next year' (2027) and expects gross margin expansion in a growth year at a '40% to 60% fall-through' [src 42], so those builds are sized and carded beside the booked 38%. FY29 38%: the 2028 supply tightness that supports pricing ends [src 42]; outside the NTM window (no value effect). KILIAN CARD 2026-11-19 (cmsg_01HdhANNPxz1f5xqDwR22cfL1UcvnBVFDqZM6obu2A4qB8, '40% fall-through from Q4 FY27'): FY2028-29 = Q4 FY27 39% plus a 40% fall-through on DCAI revenue growth with opex held, the low end of 'I still lean towards the 40% to 60% fall-through' (David Zinsner, CFO [src 42]): replaces the unsourced 38% FY28-29 level. KILIAN CARD 2026-11-24 (cmsg_01HdhANNPxz1f5xqDwR22cfLUsCc6RnFSwH3YJMmV4yvH6, 'Keep 40% fall-through (booked)'): the 40% fall-through is kept and re-chained on the new dcai_rev path (card cmsg_01HdhANNPxz1f5xqDwR22cfLFzsG6GiNiCEnTZngJoQmX1, 'Median of revised five 36.0B / 41.0B'), on the pre-moratorium dcai_rev row: OI_q = OI_q-1 + 0.40 x (R_q - R_q-1), anchored at Q4 FY27 39% on 10,100 (OI 3,939). Q1 FY28 9,688.8 gives 38.96%, Q2-Q4 10,434.1 give 39.03%, Q1 FY29 10,657.7 gives 39.05%, Q2-Q4 11,477.5 give 39.12%: FY2028 39.0%, FY2029 39.1% (FY2027 36% / 38% / 39% / 39% unchanged, 38.1% on the new quarters). The rule works both ways, so the lower Q1 FY28 revenue (a shape effect of the median build) lowers that quarter's margin slightly. As the card noted, the lower FY2028 revenue already lowers the margin through the fall-through, so no further fade is applied.

drivers.label: Gross capital expenditure (additions to PP&E, investing plus financing lines)
drivers.source: Actuals: cash-flow statements (investing additions plus financing-line additions) in the releases [16][15][13][17]: Q3 FY26 gross 4,219 in the adjusted-FCF reconciliation [13]. Guides: 2026 gross capex ~$20B, 2027 rising strongly, equipment POs +~40% q/q, no positive FCF in 2027 [23]. FY2028-29 parts: Futurum fit-out cost and 2027-2028 timing [56]; Ohio spend to date, completion and equipment lead [57]; Q3 2026 call [42].
drivers.derivation: Q4 FY26 5,907 = Q3 gross 4,219 x 1.40: firm equipment purchase orders 'increasing nearly 40% sequentially' and 'a lot of what we're spending on now is really equipment' (David Zinsner, CFO, Q3 2026 call [src 42]); FY26 = 11,834 YTD + 5,907 = 17,741. Cross-check, not the basis: Intel's FY2025 first capex guide $20.0B ended at 17,672 (-11.6% [21][17]), and FY2026 lands -11.3% under the ~$20B guide. FY27 26,000 (+47%; 6,000 / 6,500 / 6,700 / 6,800): 'up strongly' and POs +40% q/q; analysts on the call think ~$30B (Arcuri, sized as an alternative); with this capex the build gives negative FCFF in FY27, as management says. FY2028-FY2029 BUILT FROM THREE PARTS (2026-11-18 rebuild; script driver_models/INTC/carry_1118/build.py): (1) one leading-node fit-out (Fab 62 / 14A) of ~$25B for ~40k wafer starts a month, spent across 2027-2028 (Futurum, Brendan Burke, 2026-08-11 [src 56]), booked 12,500 in each year; 14A 'to begin production in 28' (Zinsner, CFO [src 42]); no second fit-out is booked for 2029 because no customer commitment or plan for one is public (Zinsner: 'we will not spend a dollar of capital unless we have confidence'), sized as an alternative. (2) Ohio: the $28B Ohio One campus (two fabs) less the >$5B spent (~$7B with contract commitments) by end-2025 leaves ~$21B (WYSU 2026-08-26 [src 57]); Intel says the first of two fabs completes by 2031 [src 57] and Licking County Commissioner Tim Bubb (not the company) cites a two-year equipment lead [src 57], so spend rises into the tool-in: 2,500 / 3,500 / 4,000 / 5,000 / 3,500 / 2,500 for 2026-2031 (sums to 21,000; booking the whole campus's remaining spend by 2031 is the set's estimate, low confidence: the page dates only the first of the two fabs, so a first-fab-only reading is sized as an alternative); 'we're still in the heavy construction phase of Ohio' (Zinsner) and Lip-Bu Tan (CEO) 'continue to evaluate ... opportunity to accelerate our Ohio build-out' [src 42], acceleration sized as an alternative. (3) Sustaining and other spend (18A/Intel 3 upkeep, packaging, other sites) = FY2027 26,000 less the fit-out 12,500 and Ohio 3,500 = 10,000, then moving with the machinery in service (machinery depreciation from the shared depreciation engine, FY27 10,818 / FY28 11,504 / FY29 12,415): FY28 10,635, FY29 11,477. FY28 = 10,635 + 12,500 + 4,000 = 27,135, split by weeks (Q1 FY2028 has 14 of 53: 7,167.7, then 6,655.7 a quarter); FY29 = 11,477 + 0 + 5,000 = 16,477 (4,119.2 a quarter, 13-week quarters) as the Fab 62 fit-out ends before Ohio's tools arrive. PREVIOUS: FY28 and FY29 27,000 each, FY29 held at the FY2028 level (carry_trace 2026-11-18). FY2028-FY2029 capex is outside the horizon cash roll and the NTM window: it moves depreciation only from FY2028 on, no value effect.
